# leaseweb_object_storage_bucket (Resource)

Manage an object storage bucket

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage an object storage bucket
resource "leaseweb_object_storage_bucket" "backups" {
  object_storage_id     = "5c9d2a1e-3b47-4f8d-9e21-7a6c8b0d4f33"
  name                  = "my-backups"
  is_versioning_enabled = true
}

# A bucket with a quota of 500 GB
resource "leaseweb_object_storage_bucket" "archive" {
  object_storage_id     = "5c9d2a1e-3b47-4f8d-9e21-7a6c8b0d4f33"
  name                  = "my-archive"
  is_versioning_enabled = false
  quota                 = 500
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `is_versioning_enabled` (Boolean) Whether versioning is enabled for the bucket
- `name` (String) Bucket name. Must be 3-63 characters, alphanumeric and hyphens only
- `object_storage_id` (String) ID of the object storage the bucket belongs to

### Optional

- `quota` (Number) Quota for the size of the bucket in GB. Omit for no quota

### Read-Only

- `creation_time` (String) The date and time the bucket was created
- `id` (String) Bucket name, used as the resource identifier
- `is_being_deleted` (Boolean) Whether the bucket is currently being deleted
- `object_count` (Number) Number of objects in the bucket
- `region` (String) Region the bucket resides in
- `used` (Attributes) Space used by the bucket (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--used))

<a id="nestedatt--used"></a>
### Nested Schema for `used`

Read-Only:

- `unit` (String) Unit of the used space, e.g. GB
- `value` (Number) Value of the used space

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A bucket can be imported by specifying the object storage ID and the bucket name in comma-separated format.
terraform import leaseweb_object_storage_bucket.example "5c9d2a1e-3b47-4f8d-9e21-7a6c8b0d4f33,my-backups"
```
